topic: Bashir Chacha's old lantern lights up by itself on the nights someone needs help.

episode.title: Midnight Watch: The Lantern Knows

shots.narration: My lantern lights itself when someone needs help.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, 3D animated film look, old Pakistani haveli courtyard at night, brass lantern between seated bashir and saad, no text.
shots.action: The unlit brass lantern ignites by itself.
shots.mood: Sudden amber light against deep blue moonlight and drifting fog.

shots.narration: Saad knew that glow better than anyone.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, haveli courtyard, bashir in grey beard, white cap and brown shawl beside saad in dark green hoodie and jeans, no text.
shots.action: Saad draws his knees away from the lantern.
shots.mood: Uneasy amber reflections across Saad's tense face.

shots.narration: [whispers] Last winter, it led me straight to him.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, lantern-lit haveli courtyard, bashir seated opposite saad beneath weathered arches, no text.
shots.action: Bashir points toward the distant railway tracks.
shots.mood: Cold mist beyond the courtyard and long trembling shadows.

shots.narration: Saad had sheltered inside an empty railway waiting room.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, flashback, deserted Pakistani railway waiting room with wooden benches and an unmarked door, no text.
shots.action: The door swings shut behind Saad.
shots.mood: Dusty moonlight, peeling plaster and deep empty corners.

shots.narration: Then the door refused to open.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, inside the railway waiting room, saad beside the closed wooden door with his small torch, no text.
shots.mood: A narrow torch beam and a motionless black window.

shots.narration: [surprised] Outside, my cold lantern suddenly burned bright.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, deserted village lane near the railway station, bashir holding his old brass lantern, no text.
shots.action: The lantern ignites in Bashir's hand.
shots.mood: Warm flame bursting through thick silver fog.

shots.narration: Its light stretched toward the station.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, village lane facing a distant unmarked railway station, bashir holding the lantern, no text.
shots.action: A narrow amber beam extends along the ground toward the station.
shots.mood: An unnatural ribbon of light beneath dark trees.

shots.narration: I followed it to a bolted door.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, deserted railway platform outside the waiting room, rusty exterior bolt visible on its wooden door, no text.
shots.action: Bashir approaches the bolted door with his lantern.
shots.mood: Empty tracks disappearing into fog behind a lonely amber glow.

shots.narration: [sighs] Someone had locked him in from outside.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, close view of the waiting-room door and its rusty exterior bolt, bashir beside it, no text.
shots.mood: Sharp lantern highlights on rust and splintered wood.

shots.narration: Saad stepped out, but his shadow stayed behind.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, open waiting-room doorway, bashir on the platform, Saad's hoodie-shaped shadow fixed on the interior wall, no text.
shots.mood: Warm safety outside contrasted with a cold, unnaturally still interior.

shots.narration: Then it waved for us to come back.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, view past motionless bashir and saad into the empty waiting room, Saad's detached shadow on the far wall, no text.
shots.action: Saad's detached shadow raises one long hand in a beckoning wave.
shots.mood: Pitch-black shadow fingers against pale plaster, lantern light fading at the thr

shots.narration: [whispers] Tonight, it points inside our sealed well.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, present-night haveli courtyard, bashir and saad beside the lantern, an old stone well covered by a heavy slab, no text.
shots.action: The lantern casts a narrow beam into a crack beneath the well's cover.
shots.mood: Amber light disappearing beneath heavy stone in silent blue fog.

episode.endHook: Who needs help beneath the sealed well?
episode.description: Bashir Chacha’s old lantern lights itself whenever someone needs help. Tonight, he tells Saad about the railway station where it first brought them together—and something that never left. A fictional spooky tale set in Pakistan.
